evidence: All five classes (ProductCreatedEvent, ProductDescriptionChangedEvent, ProductNameChangedEvent, ProductPriceChangedEvent, ProductStatusChangedEvent) extend AbstractDomainEvent and take EventMetadata as their last constructor parameter.
Every static fromJSON calls AbstractDomainEvent.extractMetadata(json) and AbstractDomainEvent.extractEventData(json), so all files use the base class helpers the same way.

ProductDescriptionChangedEvent.ts, ProductNameChangedEvent.ts, ProductPriceChangedEvent.ts and ProductStatusChanged.ts repeat assignments like this.productId = productId, which do nothing because the readonly parameter properties already set the fields. ProductCreatedEvent.ts omits them. This is cosmetic.
ProductStatusChanged.ts exports the class ProductStatusChangedEvent, so its file name does not follow the *Event.ts convention of the other four files. This is a naming issue, not a cohesion issue.
The module's only outgoing dependency is @nestjslatam/ddd-lib, and index.ts re-exports all five events as one barrel.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The five files have one concern: domain events for the Product aggregate. Every class extends AbstractDomainEvent from @nestjslatam/ddd-lib, passes EventMetadata to super, and rebuilds itself in a static fromJSON factory. Each fromJSON calls the shared helpers AbstractDomainEvent.extractMetadata and extractEventData, so no file bypasses the module's abstractions or re-implements metadata handling. The fromJSON factories have the same shape, but each one maps its own event's payload, so this is a per-event pattern rather than a shared rule copied into several places. There are two small inconsistencies, both cosmetic: (1) four constructors repeat assignments such as this.productId = productId even though the readonly parameter properties already set those fields, while ProductCreatedEvent does not; (2) the file ProductStatusChanged.ts exports ProductStatusChangedEvent, which breaks the *Event.ts file naming the other four files use. Neither one splits the module's concern, duplicates an invariant, or bypasses an abstraction, so the unit passes.
